chapter: Brass bands and the WPA band
title: Substituting in the Eureka band and sick colleagues
summary: He subbed with the Eureka band years ago when regulars were sick; they ask after Happy Goldston and Buster Moore.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh, I met about Eureka about last, seven years ago. I played the Eureka. But I wasn't considered a member of the band at that time. I just was fiddling, pain-ditting. Somebody couldn't make it such as Harold. You know, couldn't make it. He'd send me in his place. Yeah, Roddy was with him for a long time. Yeah, Roddy was beginning to get sick. I would go in his place.
Pretty nice, I heard him. He still walked with him. You haven't? He's sick. I haven't seen him in quite a while. That's what I heard in the news for them.

I haven't seen him in quite a while. I just, you know, I try to get him out of the scene, but... So many people have been sick lately. And Buster Moore lives up around here somewhere, too, doesn't he? You know him? Who is that? Buster Moore, trombone player?
I hear he's been sick, too.
Yeah. Left-handed. Yeah, that's strange to see. I looked funny when you see that.
